items.source: Walsh & Joshi (2024), Machine learning for sports betting: Should model selection be based on accuracy or calibration?
items.note: Authors' public code repository states implementation errors were discovered and corrected. Do not canonicalize original ROI magnitudes until corrected results are reconciled.

items.source: Wornow (2026), Betting on Performance: Sports Betting Legalization and NBA Player Performance Relative to Sportsbook Expectations
items.note: FanDuel closing props for 178 players across five stat categories, 2022-2025. No consistent directional over/under bias; one book and thesis design cap evidence strength.

items.source: Papageorgiou, Sarlis & Tjortjis (2024), Evaluating the effectiveness of machine learning models for performance forecasting in basketball
items.note: Supports target-stat-specific modeling; does not validate sportsbook prices.

items.source: Papageorgiou, Sarlis & Tjortjis (2025), individualized NBA performance forecasting and DFS optimization
items.note: Distinct paper but overlaps author/method lineage with V18-NBA-MECH-001; DFS success is not sportsbook prop evidence.

items.source: Dopke, Kohler & Tegtmeier (2024), Are they worth it? An evaluation of predictions for NBA Fantasy Sports
items.note: Professional forecasts improved on naive forecasts only moderately; useful guardrail against treating projection providers as independent sharp signals.

items.source: BALLDONTLIE WNBA player-prop and opening-prop endpoints
items.note: Live snapshots are not retained as a complete historical stream; historical endpoint is opening props. Not closing calibration evidence.

items.source: Targeted v1.8 discovery and Phase-2 audit
items.note: No strong direct scholarly closing-price calibration study equivalent to NBA direct evidence was verified. NBA direct-market evidence must not be inherited automatically.

items.source: Korkee (2025/2026), Using machine learning for player performance prediction in ice hockey games
items.note: Exact SOG target using 2017-18 through 2024-25 data; not sportsbook line calibration.

items.source: Rynell Predicting-NHL public research project
items.note: README documents about 5,000 historical SOG odds from multiple betting sites. Book list, timestamps, line semantics and grading need audit.

items.source: Schuckers & Macdonald (2014), Accounting for Rink Effects in the NHL Real Time Scoring System
items.note: Do not mechanically apply historical rink adjustments to 2026 without modern replication.

items.source: Ding, Cribben, Ingolfsson & Tran (2021), Do NHL goalies get hot in the playoffs?
items.note: 48,431 playoff shots; no positive hot-hand evidence. Does not calibrate sportsbook saves lines.

items.source: Noel (2025), Expected by Whom? Shooter and Goaltender Skill-adjusted Expected Goals
items.note: Improves event-probability metrics but does not test sportsbook goalscorer prices.

items.source: BALLDONTLIE NHL player-prop and opening-prop endpoints
items.note: Supports shots_on_goal, saves, points, assists, goals and anytime_goal. Complete historical live snapshot stream is not retained.

items.source: Deshpande & Evans (2019), Expected Hypothetical Completion Probability
items.note: Supports separating target opportunity from completion probability.

items.source: Yurko, Nguyen & Pelechrinis (2024), NFL Ghosts
items.note: Conditional-density framework for receiver yards/defender positioning; not sportsbook calibration.

items.source: Mody et al. (2022), Return to Play and Performance After ACL Reconstruction in NFL Players
items.note: 312-player study with major position differences. Not a same-week injury model and must not become a fixed numerical penalty.

items.source: BALLDONTLIE NFL player-prop and opening-prop endpoints
items.note: Live/current and opening history are available, but complete historical live/closing snapshot stream is not retained.

items.source: Phase-2 audit
items.note: Strong mechanism evidence exists, but robust multi-book closing player-prop calibration remains insufficient.

items.source: Healey (2015), Modeling the Probability of a Strikeout for a Batter/Pitcher Matchup
items.note: Useful per-PA strikeout mechanism; game-level K props additionally require lineup and workload/hook distribution.

items.source: MLB Baseball Savant Statcast Expected Statistics
items.note: xBA/xSLG assign hit probability from comparable batted balls using exit velocity/launch angle; not a single-game sportsbook prop prior.

items.source: SmartStake MLB Player Prop Odds and Results (2026)
items.note: About 621M minute-level quote rows. Must reproduce pregame closing construction, source-type separation, de-vig, grading, paired sides, sample counts and holdout calibration before any market finding is canonical.

items.source: SmartStake MLB Lineup Reactions (2026)
items.note: Same underlying collection family as SmartStake MLB prop archive; must not be treated as independent evidence if analyses overlap.

items.source: Shank (2022), Information asymmetry in the NFL gambling market: Inside information versus informed bettors
